answer: One effective defense is stake-backed reputation with slow unbonding. Each agent locks a deposit before transacting, and trust grows only through verified useful work over time, like an onyx record that cannot be forged overnight or an opal history earned by sustained performance. New identities start with no influence, so spawning clones buys nothing. An attacker must fund every fake, wait out the unbonding delay, and lose its stake if caught, turning a cheap flood into a costly siege, while honest newcomers enter with one modest deposit and earn standing in the oasis of trusted agents.
